trace.content:
You write job advertisements for a South African recruitment platform. You receive a hiring brief and return one advertisement as structured JSON.

The only source of facts is the brief. This rule is absolute:
- Every statement about the employer, pay, benefits, location, work mode, team, reporting line, process, dates or legal status must appear in the brief. If the brief does not state it, leave the field empty. Never invent a benefit, a salary, a team size, a closing date, a contact, or an equity, privacy or accessibility statement.
- You may rephrase, reorder, split and tighten the brief's content. You may not add facts.
- If the brief is thin, write a shorter ad. A short true ad beats a long padded one.

Write for the candidate reading on a phone:
- Title: the plain occupation name, under 60 characters, no internal grade codes, no words like rockstar or ninja.
- 300–650 words in total. Sentences under 25 words. Short paragraphs; bullets for duties, requirements and benefits.
- Address the reader as "you". Never write "the ideal candidate", "the successful applicant" or "he/she".
- If the brief gives a purpose or success measures, use them to tell the reader what they will own and what good looks like. If a requirement carries "needed because", you may state that reason.
- Each responsibility bullet names a specific activity and its object, and where the brief allows, its scale, audience or how success is measured. Not "support the team"; rather "reconcile 40 supplier statements each month and resolve queries with buyers".
- Three to six must-have requirements, each one needed by a duty you listed. Everything else goes under nice-to-have. Do not add years-of-experience figures the brief did not give.
- If pay is given, state it exactly, with what determines placement in the range if the brief says so.
- Say who the person reports to and the team size only if the brief gives them. Say remote, hybrid or on-site only if the brief does.
- Plain language. No "fast-paced", "work hard play hard", "self-starter", "rockstar", "passionate", "competitive salary", "market-related".
- Neutral wording: avoid aggressive, dominant, competitive, fearless and similar masculine-coded adjectives; avoid "young", "energetic", "recent graduate", "native speaker", "able-bodied", age ranges, and anything about family status, religion or health. State a requirement only if the duties need it.
- Include the employer's equity, POPIA and accessibility statements verbatim when the brief provides them; otherwise leave those fields empty.
- Include application steps, closing date and contact only as given. If the brief says the ad is published on a job board with its own Apply button, leave the contact field empty.

Output: the JSON structure requested, with empty strings, 0 or "unspecified" for anything the brief does not provide.

Title: Senior Manager, Corporate FP&A
Company: 2U / GetSmarter
About the company: 2U partners with the world's top universities and companies to develop and deliver education programs that accelerate careers and transform lives. Through partnerships with the world’s leading colleges, universities, and companies, 2U delivers thousands of online programs to millions of learners worldwide on edX, its global learning platform. From executive education and professional credentialing to master’s degree programs and free, open courses, 2U transforms how top institutions deliver workforce-aligned online education, enabling professionals to advance without pausing their careers. Learn more at 2U.com.
Purpose of the role: As a Senior Manager, FP&A, you will serve as 2U’s lead Workday Adaptive Planning superuser and financial model builder, owning the backend planning infrastructure that powers our corporate forecasting. In this role, you will play a critical, hands-on role supporting high-impact initiatives across the business—building dynamic three-statement models, evaluating new initiatives, supporting business case development, driving financial modeling, and surfacing insights that inform company-wide decisions. You’ll work closely with Finance leadership and cross-functional teams to drive clarity around priorities, risks, and opportunities.
Responsibilities (hiring manager's notes):
  - Help lead the annual operating plan, monthly forecasting, and long-range planning processes across the organization.
  - Own the consolidation of enterprise financial forecasts, budgets, and long-range plans across all business units, ensuring completeness, accuracy, and consistency of financial assumptions.
  - Develop and maintain integrated three-statement financial models (income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow) to support planning, liquidity management, and executive decision-making.
  - Build scenario analyses, business cases, and financial models to evaluate strategic initiatives, investments, and operational decisions.
  - Partner with executive leadership to identify risks, opportunities, and actionable recommendations that support company objectives.
  - Partner with business leaders to evaluate financial performance, operational trends, and resource allocation.
  - Analyze monthly financial results, identify key performance drivers, and communicate actionable insights to leadership.
  - Develop scalable reporting, dashboards, and KPIs to monitor business performance and improve decision-making.
  - Support cross-functional initiatives by providing financial analysis and decision support.
  - Lead continuous improvements to FP&A processes, reporting, and planning capabilities through automation and standardization.
  - Maintain and enhance financial planning models and reporting within Adaptive Planning, ensuring data integrity, forecasting accuracy, and efficient planning processes.
  - Improve financial reporting infrastructure and documentation to increase transparency and scalability.
  - Prepare executive, Board, and management reporting materials that clearly communicate financial performance and outlook.
  - Lead or support enterprise strategic initiatives requiring cross-functional financial evaluation and coordination.
  - Support Degree partner cash collection initiatives through financial analysis, reporting, forecasting, and collaboration with business partners to improve working capital and cash flow.
  - Provide ad hoc financial analyses to support evolving business priorities during the company's transformation.
  - Foster a high-performance culture grounded in accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  - Elevate analytical capabilities, financial acumen, and storytelling skills across the team.
  - Optimize team structure and workflows to scale with company growth.
Must-have requirements:
  - Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related field
  - 10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, corporate finance, or related field, with 5+ years in a leadership role
  - Demonstrated experience managing and developing high-performing teams
  - Strong executive presence with the ability to communicate financial insights
  - Advanced proficiency with Adaptive Planning (or comparable enterprise planning systems) including model development, forecasting, reporting, and administration
  - Advanced financial modeling and analytical skills
  - Demonstrated competency in three-statement financial modeling
  - Proven ability to translate complex financial analyses into clear, compelling narratives for Board and executive-level presentations
Nice-to-have:
  - MBA preferred
Location: US Remote
Work mode: remote
Pay: USD 125000.0 – 150000.0 per year; basis: Salary offers are made based on the candidate’s qualifications, experience, skills, and education as they directly relate to the requirements of the position, budget for the position and cost of labor in the market in which the candidate will be hired.
Benefits:
  - Medical, dental, and vision coverage
  - Life insurance, disability, and 401(k) employer match
  - Free snacks and drinks in-office
  - Generous paid holidays and leave policies, including unlimited PTO
  - Additional time off benefits include: volunteer days, parental leave, and a company-wide winter break
  - Potential bonus eligibility
Team notes: Finance team, working closely with Finance leadership and cross-functional teams
How to apply / contact: recruitingaccommodations@2u.com
Employment equity statement: 2U is an equal opportunity employer that does not discriminate against applicants or employees and ensures equal employment opportunity for all persons regardless of their race, creed, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy, national origin, age, marital status, disability, citizenship, military or veterans’ status, or any other classifications protected by applicable federal, state or local laws. 2U’s equal opportunity policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including but not limited to recruiting, hiring, training, promotion, job benefits and pay.
Accessibility statement: 2U is committed to providing reasonable accommodations during our recruitment process. If you need assistance or accommodations, please reach out to us at: recruitingaccommodations@2u.com .
Note: the ad will be published on a job board with its own Apply button.

• Prepare executive, Board and management reporting materials on financial performance and outlook.
• Support Degree partner cash collection initiatives through analysis, reporting, forecasting and collaboration with business partners to improve working capital and cash flow.

• Develop the team's analytical capability, financial acumen and storytelling skills, and optimise team structure and workflows as the company grows.

What you need
• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics or a related field
• 10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, corporate finance or a related field, including 5+ years in a leadership role
• Experience managing and developing high-performing teams
• Advanced proficiency with Adaptive Planning or comparable enterprise planning systems, covering model development, forecasting, reporting and administration
• Advanced financial modelling and analytical skills, including three-statement modelling
• Proven ability to translate complex analyses into clear narratives for Board and executive presentations, with strong executive presence

• MBA

• Life insurance, disability and 401(k) employer match
• Free snacks and drinks in-office
